Q: How to properly store image dimensions in Django A:

Django’s ImageField has two built-in parameters specifically designed for this. When you upload an image, Django automatically extracts the dimensions and populates the designated fields.

The Implementation of possible solution

from django.db import models

class MyModel(models.Model):
    image = models.ImageField(
        upload_path='uploads/',
        width_field='image_width',   # Reference to the field name
        height_field='image_height'  # Reference to the field name
    )
    # These fields must exist; Django fills them automatically
    image_width = models.PositiveIntegerField(null=True, blank=True, editable=False)
    image_height = models.PositiveIntegerField(null=True, blank=True, editable=False)

Q: Looking for a low-code / no-code platform to build a scalable MVP without heavy infrastructure or dev costs A:

Two things that have worked well for me:

Azure Container Apps (biased — it's what I know best, AWS/GCP will get you to the same place)

Deploy your container and mostly forget about the infra. Scales to zero when idle so you're not paying for nothing, and it doesn't fall over when multiple users hit it at once. Free tier is fine for early validation.

Self-hosted Docker on a cheap VPS

Hetzner, ~$10/month. Docker Compose locally, same thing in prod, Caddy in front for HTTPS. Simple, cheap, and if you ever need to scale you're already containerized so there's nothing to rewrite.

The actual problem with Replit/Lovable isn't the generated code - it's that they hide the infrastructure from you entirely. Take whatever they produce, containerize it, and most of those stability issues go away.

Heroku used to be the obvious answer here but that was before they killed the free tier.

Honestly though: just use whatever cloud you already know. At MVP stage the learning curve costs more than any price difference.

Q: Are there any real difference between GlobalScope and CoroutineScope? A:

The CoroutineScope function creates a Job if there isn't one in the context you pass.

So,

GlobalScope.cancel() // does nothing
yourScope.cancel()  // cancels all the tasks launched in this scope

Except for that, CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Default) is identical to GlobalScope.

Q: How can I avoid IEnumerable nested in another IEnumerable using lambda expressions A:

Since nobody wanted to post the answer besides in a comment (thank you for that), I thought I will post it here myself:

You can use SelectMany instead of Select to flatten the nested IEnumerable<IEnumerable<Type>> into a single IEnumerable<Type>:

var types = assemblies.SelectMany(asm => asm.GetExportedTypes()
                        .Where(t => typeof(IMyCustomValidator).IsAssignableFrom(t) && !t.IsInterface));

Select maps each element to one result (hence the nesting), while SelectMany maps each element to a sequence and merges them all into a flat result.
